language_wrapper: Consider a regular {num_sides}-prism. On each lateral rectangular face, draw both face diagonals and let their intersection be a point. Remove all lateral edges of the prism, but keep the base polygon edges. Additionally, connect each such intersection point to the intersection points of the two adjacent lateral faces, forming a cycle of intersection points around the prism. On the resulting graph whose vertices are the 2{num_sides} base vertices and the {num_sides} intersection points, perform a proper {num_colors}-coloring (adjacent vertices cannot share a color). Two colorings are considered the same if one is obtained from the other by a rotation about the prism’s axis. Determine the number of such inequivalent colorings.
hardness_rationale: Compared to the seed, the augmented family adds a new cycle of intersection points, creating three interlinked rings (top, bottom, centers) with nearest-neighbor and cross constraints. Counting proper colorings up to rotational symmetry now requires Burnside’s lemma together with a nontrivial transfer-matrix method over a state space of size k(k−1)^2. The adjacency constraints couple consecutive blocks via both top/bottom transitions and center-to-neighbor restrictions, preventing simple decoupling or naive recurrence; the computation must handle weighted closed walks on a directed state graph and aggregate over all rotation periods via the gcd structure.
notes: Proof sketch: Model the graph as three cyclic layers indexed mod n: top T_i, bottom B_i, and centers M_i. Edges are T_i−T_{i+1}, B_i−B_{i+1}, M_i−M_{i+1}, and for each i, M_i adjacent to T_i, T_{i+1}, B_i, B_{i+1}. We count proper colorings modulo rotations using Burnside’s lemma. A rotation by t positions fixes exactly those colorings that are periodic with period d = gcd(n, t), i.e., colors depend only on the index mod d. This reduces the problem to counting colorings of a length-d cycle with the same local constraints and wrap-around. Encode each position j by a state s_j = (T_j, B_j, M_j) with the intra-position constraint M_j ≠ T_j and M_j ≠ B_j. Adjacency between successive positions enforces T_j ≠ T_{j+1}, B_j ≠ B_{j+1}, M_j ≠ M_{j+1}, and cross constraints M_j ≠ T_{j+1}, M_j ≠ B_{j+1}, M_{j+1} ≠ T_j, M_{j+1} ≠ B_j. Let S be the set of valid states; |S| = k(k−1)^2 (for each (t,b), m has k−|{t,b}| options). Construct the adjacency matrix A over S with entries A_{uv} = 1 if u and v satisfy the inter-position constraints, and 0 otherwise. Then the number of length-d cyclic colorings fixed by the rotation is exactly Tr(A^d), the number of closed walks of length d in the state graph. Burnside’s lemma yields the orbit count under rotations as (1/n) * sum_{t=0}^{n−1} Tr(A^{gcd(n,t)}). Grouping by d = gcd(n, t), the sum simplifies to (1/n) * sum_{d|n} φ(n/d) Tr(A^d). The verifier computes this expression exactly via integer matrix exponentiation, ensuring correctness and nontriviality. This approach generalizes seamlessly in parameters n and k and cannot be solved by guesswork due to the coupled constraints and symmetry averaging.
source_question: Consider a regular 25-prism. By connecting the face diagonals of each lateral face, 25 intersection points are generated, and then the lateral edges are removed. Now, we perform a three-coloring on these 25 intersection points and 50 vertices, where adjacent vertices cannot have the same color. Colorings that coincide after rotation around the central axis are regarded as the same kind. Find the number of coloring methods.
